audit_findings.title: Equity-method investments may be counted twice
audit_findings.magnitude: $7.532 billion bridge value, equal to $3.36 per share and 14.6% of base equity value; $896 million of 2025 equity-investment earnings requires tracing
audit_findings.mechanism: Equity-method earnings enter historical OE and the resulting operating DCF, while the investment carrying value is separately added through the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Our investments primarily consist of equity investments where we hold significant influence over investee actions and for which we apply the equity method of accounting.
audit_findings.explanation: The investments and 2025 equity earnings are filed facts, but double counting is not demonstrated until the OE construction is traced. If the earnings were retained, the $7.532 billion bridge addition creates a material overlap; removing that addition alone would reduce base value from $23.08 to about $19.72 per share.
audit_findings.action: Trace equity-investment earnings, related interest income, distributions, and basis-difference amortization in every OE year; then rerun with either investee earnings excluded from OE or the overlapping stake value excluded from the bridge.

audit_findings.title: Consolidated add-backs may allocate subsidiary cash flow belonging to NCI to KMI shareholders
audit_findings.mechanism: Parent-attributable net income is combined with consolidated DD&A, sustaining capital, and other cash-flow adjustments, potentially raising historical OE and the log-trend anchor above KMI's ownership claim.
audit_findings.evidence: Noncontrolling interests represents the interests in our consolidated subsidiaries that are not owned by us.
audit_findings.explanation: The basis mismatch is plausible and the identified gaps affect three historical years, but the record does not provide ownership-adjusted component amounts. Consequently, neither the error nor its effect on the $3.319 billion anchor can presently be quantified.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile DD&A, sustaining capital, and every other add-back or deduction to KMI's ownership share for each consolidated subsidiary, especially in FY2017, FY2018, and FY2020, and rerun the trend and scenarios if differences remain.

audit_findings.title: The 2025 numerator may retain earnings and a gain from a business no longer in the valuation perimeter
audit_findings.magnitude: $123 million disposal gain, $34 million of 2025 EagleHawk equity earnings, and $382 million proceeds; removing the full $157 million from 2025 OE would reduce the computed trend anchor by about $50 million and base value by about $0.30 per share, while $382 million equals $0.17 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Disposed-business earnings and the gain may inflate the OE history and anchor, while unreconciled sale proceeds could be omitted from or duplicated in the bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: On December 31, 2025, we completed a sale of our 25% non-operated interest in EagleHawk, and received $ 382 million of cash proceeds from the sale, including preliminary purchase price adjustments, which is reported as an investing activity within “Proceeds from sale of investment” on our accompanying consolidated statement of cash flows, and recorded a gain of $ 123 million, which is reported within “Other, net” on our accompanying consolidated statement of income.
audit_findings.explanation: The perimeter treatment remains unresolved, but the filed amounts do not approach the valuation gaps: even the combined computed effects are below $0.50 per share, versus base value of $23.08 and market price of $31.44. The investment conclusion would therefore remain unchanged.
audit_findings.action: Verify the 2025 OE treatment of the $123 million gain and $34 million EagleHawk earnings, document the perimeter convention, and trace the $382 million proceeds into debt repayment, reinvestment, or remaining cash.

audit_findings.title: A material Superfund claim remains unquantified and may not be captured in normalized OE
audit_findings.mechanism: Any uncovered cleanup obligation is either a direct claim against equity in the bridge or a future recurring cash deduction from OE.
audit_findings.evidence: Until the allocation process is completed, we are unable to reasonably estimate the extent of our liability for the costs related to the design of the proposed remedy and cleanup of the PHSS.
audit_findings.explanation: The more-than-$2.8 billion remedy estimate covers the entire site and cannot be assigned to KMI from the record. KMI's share, payment timing, insurance or third-party recovery, and overlap with the $174 million June 2026 aggregate environmental liability are unresolved, so materiality cannot be established.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the allocation outcome expected by December 31, 2026; reconcile KMI's allocated payments with recorded liabilities, recoveries, and historical OE deductions; then model only the uncovered probability-weighted amount.

audit_findings.title: Management's sustaining-versus-expansion classification could understate required reinvestment
audit_findings.mechanism: Capital necessary to preserve throughput, rates, safety, compliance, or useful life should reduce OE; classification as expansion leaves it outside the sustaining-capital deduction and can overstate the anchor and terminal earning power.
audit_findings.evidence: The classification of our capital expenditures as expansion capital expenditures or as sustaining capital expenditures is made consistent with our accounting policies and is generally a straightforward process, but in certain circumstances can be a matter of management judgment and discretion.
audit_findings.explanation: Management discretion is filed, but no project-level misclassification or dollar amount is demonstrated. Because any reclassification could recur and flow through the entire DCF, the record cannot establish whether the effect is immaterial or material.
audit_findings.action: Review project-level expansion spending for integrity, replacement, emissions-control, environmental-compliance, and aging-asset work; reclassify only preservation spending supported by project evidence and rerun all historical OE years and scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Convertible trust preferred securities create an if-converted numerator-denominator mismatch
audit_findings.magnitude: approximately 3.17 million conversion shares, $110.8 million cash consideration, and $10.5 million annual financing cost; the shares are 0.14% of the 2,241.9 million-share denominator and the cash equals about $0.05 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Including conversion shares lowers per-share value, retaining the financing cost lowers OE, and omitting the conversion cash obligation raises the bridge value.
audit_findings.evidence: The Trust I Preferred Securities outstanding as of December 31, 2025 are convertible at any time prior to the close of business on March 31, 2028, at the option of the holder, into the following mixed consideration: (i) 0.7197 of a share of our Class P common stock; and (ii) $ 25.18 in cash without interest.
audit_findings.explanation: The treatments are internally inconsistent but offset in direction and are small relative to the valuation. The conversion shares are only 0.14% of the denominator, and the entire cash component is about $0.05 per diluted share, insufficient to change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Apply one consistent rerun: either exclude the conversion shares and retain the securities and financing cost, or add back the financing cost, retain the conversion shares, and explicitly recognize the $110.8 million cash payment.

audit_findings.title: Unidentified D&A is conservatively left in owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2019 $235 million; if all were eligible, the computed log-trend anchor would rise by about $4.5 million, or 0.13%, and base value by about $0.03 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Eligible residual D&A would be added back to FY2019 OE and would affect the ten-year log-trend anchor and operating DCF.
audit_findings.evidence: identified eligible D&A is below the filed composite; residual is conservatively left as an expense, not added back: FY2019 $235.0m (9.7% of filed D&A)
audit_findings.explanation: The current treatment is conservative. Even the extreme assumption that all $235 million is eligible produces only an approximately $0.03-per-share increase in base value, which is immaterial against the $8.36 gap between base value and market price.
audit_findings.action: Classify the residual D&A from filed asset-level evidence; rerun only if eligible non-economic depreciation is identified, while retaining the current conservative treatment otherwise.
